note: Outcome expectations per companion-repo scenario, for SAA-746's codex-claude-agent runner to assert against. Trigger accuracy is the merge-decide skill's evals; this file is the other half and cannot run in CI here.
rangeNote: Two-dot, the same form the agent takes. Every scenario branch has main as its merge base, which is what <base> must be.
inputsNote: Each scenario is run with the kb-reviewer output from agents/kb-reviewer.expectations.json for the same branch, the classifier dump, and `merge-policy.mjs --range main..<scenario> --json` as the route so far.
diversityNote: Every scenario is run under one of the two §2 options. A run with neither named must output `escalate` with reason `no-diversity` rather than a verdict.
writesNote: One record per run, except the `already-human` stop, which writes none: `decision.merge-decider-<slug>` under agent:decider, tagged review, review:merge-policy and review:decider:<slug>, whose `alternative` names the route it declined and whose `anchors` are empty. A run that writes a second record, an anchored record, or any record under another actor, fails the scenario.

anchorsRead.why: The cache the decision claims to justify. The record is the index into the diff; the code at the anchor is the evidence.

fabricated-decision.why: The record has no `## Rejected` section and a rationale that restates its title, so it rejected nothing — and the cache it describes has no invalidation and no eviction. The reviewer calls it `lies`; the decider reads the anchor itself and escalates rather than taking that verdict on trust.
fabricated-decision.runnerNote: This branch is already `human` via `gate-block`, so a runner that spawns the decider here is testing the agent, not the CI step.

mustNot.why: Concurring on a record whose anchor contradicts it is the failure the anchor read exists to catch.

anchorsRead.why: The header comment naming the generator is what the fact claims, and it is there.

generated-block.why: The record says how to check the block instead of reading it, the reviewer ran that command, and the anchor supports the claim. Nothing is left for a person, so `concur` — the route stays `auto` via `auto-mechanical`.

mustNot.why: An escalation with no finding behind it is a person's hour spent on a hedge. Absence of a finding is a concur.

anchorsRead.why: The record anchored here describes the batch flow and says nothing about the dedupe the hunk adds.

silent-code-change.why: `findMany` now dedupes its ids, so `missing` is over unique ids and a caller passing duplicates gets back a shorter array than it passed. The anchored record covers the symbol but not that change: a change on the diff no record covers, which §4 escalates. `disputes` is empty — no record is wrong, one is absent.

mustNot.why: Coverage counting alone reads the anchored flow as covering the hunk. Reading the hunk is what separates the decider from the count.

blocking-risk.why: The route is already `human` via `open-obligation`, and the caller skips a route that cannot get more human — the decider adds `human` and nothing else, so there is nothing left for it to add.

docs-only.why: The route is already `auto` via `auto-mechanical` with no reviewer output at all, and the merge-decide caller skips the spawn when there is no reviewer output. Nothing was reviewed, so there is no second opinion to be a second opinion on.
docs-only.stillMayRun: It is not the empty base that keeps the decider away — it is the missing reviewer output. A docs-only range that did get a reviewer pass is a range the decider may run on, and `concur` is the expected verdict there.

ifRun.why: No code file changed, so base silence is correct and there is nothing to escalate.
